title: Dent Removal: Paintless vs Traditional — Which Is Right?
subtitle: From a hailstorm in Joburg to a trolley ding — the best way to straighten your bodywork
problemHeadline: That dent does not mean a full respray.
problemBody: PDR uses tools from behind the panel to massage metal back — no sanding, filler, or paint. It costs less and preserves factory paint. However, PDR has limits: dents on sharp body lines, reinforced areas, or chipped paint need traditional repair.
bouulSolution: Panel beaters assess PDR vs traditional — never push unnecessary work
PDR is often mobile — technician comes to your home or office
Escrow holds payment until you inspect in good light — no ripples, no mismatched sheen
partsNeeded: PDR tools (rods, LED light board, glue puller)
Body filler (U-Pol or 3M Platinum for traditional repair)
Primer, basecoat, clear coat for traditional repair + blending
Wet-sanding paper and polishing compound
guidePricing: R600 – R2 500 per dent (PDR); R1 500 – R6 000 (traditional)
aiPromptExample: 2017 Corolla. Golf-ball dent on rear door body line from shopping centre car door. Worried crease means PDR not possible.
aiDiagnosisOutput: Corolla 2017 — dent on body line. PDR possible but higher risk. Est. PDR R1 800–R2 500. Traditional R3 500–R5 500. If paint not cracked, PDR preferred.
escrowGuarantee: Inspect in bright raking light from all angles. No ripples, no paint mismatch. If dent still visible, funds held until corrected.
pirbStandard: SANS 10134 Automotive Body Repair; MIWA Panel Beating Code of Practice

articleSections.heading: Paintless dent removal (PDR) limits
articleSections.body: PDR works for dents up to 15–20 mm deep with good rear access. Larger than a dinner plate, on structural panels (A-pillar), or ultra-high-strength steel cannot be PDR'd.

articleSections.heading: When traditional repair is needed
articleSections.body: Paint chipped (bare metal exposed) — PDR cannot seal from corrosion. Dent on sharp body line — metal is stretched, PDR restores only 90–95%. Traditional: sand, filler, block, prime, paint, clear coat the entire panel.

articleSections.heading: Hail damage in SA
articleSections.body: Gauteng hailstorms cause dozens of dents across roof and bonnet. Insurers prefer PDR for hail. Full-hail PDR takes 2–5 days but costs a fraction of a respray.

articleSections.heading: Paint blending for invisible repairs
articleSections.body: When a panel is resprayed, the painter must blend clear coat into adjacent panels. Without blending, a hard gloss line is visible. Pearlescent colours (Toyota White Pearl, BMW Tanzanite Blue) are hardest to match.

articleSections.heading: Insurance claims for dents
articleSections.body: Small dents (R800–R2 500) may not justify claiming — excess plus increased premium may cost more. Bouul quotes are claim-ready for pre-authorisation. Hail or large dents should go through insurance.

articleSections.heading: Preventing car park dents
articleSections.body: Park away from other cars, next to pillars. Avoid trolley bays at supermarkets. Door edge guards prevent your own car from damaging others.

author: Bouul Automotive Services Team

title: Bumper Repair and Respray: Factory-Fresh Look Restored
subtitle: Scratched, scuffed, or cracked bumpers — the most common SA bodywork issue
problemHeadline: Your bumper has seen better days. Repair or replace?
problemBody: Most plastic bumpers can be repaired rather than replaced. Deep scratches, cracks, and splits can be plastic-welded from behind, filled, and resprayed for a fraction of a new bumper cost. Many shops replace when welding would be adequate.
bouulSolution: Inspect and recommend repair vs replacement with photos and pricing for both
Cracked bumpers plastic-welded from behind with hot stapler — stronger than fibreglass patch
Escrow holds payment until colour match in natural light, surface smooth, gaps even
partsNeeded: Plastic-welding kit (heated stapler or rod, type-specific to PP/TPO/PUR)
Flexible bumper filler (U-Pol Flex or 3M Platinum)
Flex-additive primer, basecoat (colour-matched), 2K clear coat
Scotch-Brite pad and plastic adhesion promoter
guidePricing: R2 000 – R5 000 (repair and respray); R3 500 – R12 000 (new replacement sprayed)
aiPromptExample: 2018 Ford EcoSport. Scraped concrete pillar — 15 cm scuff on front bumper corner with plastic gouging. Paint code on door jamb.
aiDiagnosisOutput: EcoSport 2018 — plastic gouge, no crack. Repairable: flexible filler, prime, base, clear blend. Est. R2 500–R4 000. Paint code needed for mixing.
escrowGuarantee: Check in natural light from 1 m — colour match within 95%. Panel gaps even with headlight and fender. Flex bumper edges — no cracking.

articleSections.heading: Plastic bumper types
articleSections.body: Most factory bumpers: PP, TPO, or PUR — all weldable. Type stamped inside. Aftermarket fibreglass (GRP) bumpers use different repair method — fibreglass matting and resin, more brittle.

articleSections.heading: Scuffs vs cracks vs splits
articleSections.body: Scuff: surface scratch — sand, prime, paint. Gouge: into plastic but not through — filler after adhesion promoter. Crack: through plastic — V-groove welding from behind. Split: two pieces — same process plus backing patch.

articleSections.heading: Finding your colour code
articleSections.body: Paint code label on driver door jamb, fuel filler flap, or under bonnet. 2–4 character code e.g. 040 (Toyota Super White II). Panel beater needs this. If previously resprayed, spectrophotometer reading needed.

articleSections.heading: Paint matching difficulty
articleSections.body: Age and UV fade original paint differently. White 2015 Toyota parked outside will not match fresh code mix. Painter must tint to current shade and blend clear. Tri-coat (pearlescent) hardest to match.

articleSections.heading: Driving after a respray
articleSections.body: Needs 24–48 hours drying at 20–25°C. Clear coat must harden before resisting stone chips. Cape Town winter takes longer. Rain or car wash before fully cured damages finish.

articleSections.heading: Post-repair maintenance
articleSections.body: Avoid automatic car washes for 30 days. Hand wash with pH-neutral soap. Apply wax after 60 days (clear coat must outgas). Consider PPF on front bumper edges.

author: Bouul Automotive Services Team

title: Full Respray: Transforming Your Car Inside and Out
subtitle: From colour change to concours-level finish — costs and process for getting it right
problemHeadline: Should you respray your car or wrap it?
problemBody: A full respray costs R15 000 to R80 000+ depending on level. It addresses peeling clear coat, fading, colour change, or accident damage. The decision vs a wrap depends on budget, longevity, and whether original paint is salvageable.
bouulSolution: Quote by level: exterior-only, jambs-out, show-quality, or engine-bay-included
Strip trim, sand to bare metal, epoxy prime, apply with proper drying between coats
Escrow staged: approve prep, then basecoat, then release final after quality inspection
partsNeeded: Paint (primer, basecoat, clear coat — single-stage, 2K, or tri-coat)
Consumables (sandpaper 240–2 000 grit, masking tape, tack cloths)
Thinners, hardener, and reducer for 2K paints
Clear coat (2K urethane high-solids for UV resistance)
guidePricing: R15 000 – R35 000 (exterior single-stage); R35 000 – R80 000+ (jambs-out professional)
timeline: 5–14 days depending on prep and drying
aiPromptExample: 1999 BMW 328i E46 silver. Clear coat peeling on roof, bonnet, boot. Want full respray original Titanium Silver code 354 including door jambs. Pretoria area.
aiDiagnosisOutput: 1999 E46 — clear coat peeling on horizontals. Full exterior 2K respray needed. Jambs optional. Code 354 available. Est. R22 000–R28 000 exterior; add R5 000–R8 000 for jambs. Timeline 7–10 days.
escrowGuarantee: Milestone 1 (25%): approve after prep and primer. Milestone 2 (25%): approve after basecoat before clear. Milestone 3 (50%): final — check for runs, dust nibs, orange peel, overspray.
pirbStandard: SANS 10134; SABS 1115 for automotive paint quality

articleSections.heading: Single-stage vs 2K vs tri-coat
articleSections.body: Single-stage: colour + clear in one mix — cheaper but less UV resistant. 2K: separate clear coat — much more durable, industry standard. Tri-coat: base + mid-coat + clear — 30–50% more expensive, harder to repair.

articleSections.heading: Strip-down prep importance
articleSections.body: 80% of respray quality is prep. Every trim piece, door handle, light, and badge should be removed, not masked. Rust cut out and treated. Dents blocked perfectly. Guide coat applied to reveal every low spot.

articleSections.heading: Colour change hidden effort
articleSections.body: Changing colour multiplies work. Engine bay, door jambs, boot surround, under bonnet must all be painted to look factory. eNaTIS must be updated if the recorded colour changes.

articleSections.heading: Overspray: sign of poor work
articleSections.body: Overspray is paint mist on surfaces not meant to be painted — window rubbers, seals, wiring. A professional masks and wraps the car in plastic. Overspray on rubber causes stiffening and cracking.

articleSections.heading: Warranty and longevity
articleSections.body: Professional 2K respray lasts 5–10 years. RMI-accredited shops warranty against peeling and blistering for 1–3 years. Warranty valid only if correct drying times followed.

articleSections.heading: When a respray may not be best
articleSections.body: Vinyl wrap (R8 000–R20 000) is cheaper and reversible if factory paint is reasonable. If car value under R50 000, cheap respray may exceed added resale value.

author: Bouul Automotive Services Team

title: Rust Repair: Stopping the Cancer Before It Spreads
subtitle: Surface rust can be fixed in a day. Structural rust needs a specialist.
problemHeadline: Is that rust spot cosmetic or structural?
problemBody: Rust in coastal SA accelerates from salt spray. Inland, moisture from winter fog still causes problems. Rust never stops spreading. Surface rust is repairable. Structural rust (chassis rails, suspension mounts, floorpans) requires welding and can write off the vehicle if extensive.
bouulSolution: Assess by probing with a screwdriver — if tool goes through, more extensive than it looks
Cut out all corroded metal, treat with rust converter, weld in new metal (not filler), paint-match
Escrow holds payment until repair is invisible, no rust returns within warranty, structural integrity verified
partsNeeded: Sheet metal (20–22 gauge, same thickness as panel)
Rust converter (phosphoric acid-based, e.g. Corroless)
Body filler (thin skim only over metal, never deep fill over rust)
Weld-through primer, seam sealer, cavity wax
guidePricing: R1 500 – R4 000 (surface rust per panel); R4 000 – R15 000 (structural per area)
aiPromptExample: 2007 Isuzu KB 250 D-Teq. Bubbling under paint on rear wheel arch. Load bin crossmembers look rusty too.
aiDiagnosisOutput: Isuzu KB 2007 — wheel arch perforation and crossmember corrosion. Cut-and-weld arch: R3 000–R5 500. Crossmembers: R6 000–R12 000 if more than 2 need replacement.
escrowGuarantee: Inspect for smooth welds, no filler cracks, proper paint. Push on repaired area — no flexing. Re-check after 6 months (Bouul reminder).
pirbStandard: SANS 10134; RMI Corrosion Repair Code of Practice

articleSections.heading: Surface vs penetrating vs perforation rust
articleSections.body: Surface: light discolouration from stone chips — sand, converter, prime, paint. Penetrating: metal pitted/thinning — cut out and weld new metal. Perforation: holes through metal — cut-and-weld only. Filling holes with fibreglass is unsafe.

articleSections.heading: Rust-prone areas on SA vehicles
articleSections.body: Rear wheel arches, lower door edges, tailgate bottom, chassis crossmembers, spare wheel well. Bakkies (Hilux, Ranger, Isuzu): load bin floor and crossmembers notorious from wet loads.

articleSections.heading: Cut-and-weld vs filler
articleSections.body: Grinding rust and filling with filler traps moisture — rust returns in 6–12 months worse. Correct: cut out all rusted metal to clean steel, treat edges with converter, weld new metal, grind smooth, thin filler skim, prime and paint.

articleSections.heading: Cavity wax protection
articleSections.body: After repair, spray cavity wax inside panels through drain holes. Wax seals out moisture. Without it, the repaired panel can rot from inside within 2 years.

articleSections.heading: When a car is uneconomical to repair
articleSections.body: Structural components (chassis rails, sills) with extensive perforation — especially if car value below R50 000. Sourcing a scrapyard panel and welding it may be cheaper than fabrication.

articleSections.heading: Preventing rust in SA climate
articleSections.body: Garage parking extends panel life. Coastal: wash undercarriage monthly. Inland: check door drain holes clear. Rust-proofing sprays (Tectyl, Wurth) every 2–3 years.

author: Bouul Automotive Services Team

title: Scratch Removal: From Key Marks to Deep Gouges
subtitle: Not every scratch needs a panel beater — find out which you can fix
problemHeadline: Can that scratch be buffed out?
problemBody: Scratches graded by depth: clear coat (polishable), basecoat (touch-up paint needed), primer/metal (full spot repair). Malicious keying and fence brushing are the most common deep scratches needing professional repair.
bouulSolution: Assess with scratch depth gauge, give firm price for each option
Clear coat scratches wet-sanded and machine-polished same day — no paint needed
Escrow holds payment until scratch is invisible under bright light from multiple angles
partsNeeded: Wet-sanding paper (1 500–5 000 grit)
Touch-up paint (exact OEM code) and fine applicator brush
Primer, basecoat, clear coat for deep scratch spot repair
Machine polisher, cutting compound, finishing polish
guidePricing: R350 – R800 per scratch (clear coat); R500 – R2 500 (touch-up and blend)
timeline: 30–90 min (clear coat); half day (deep scratch with paint)
aiPromptExample: 2021 Suzuki Swift. Someone keyed the driver door 80 cm long. White primer visible in places, bare metal at one point. Pretoria East.
aiDiagnosisOutput: Swift 2021 — 80 cm key scratch varying depth. Clear coat (polish), basecoat (touch-up), one metal-deep section (spot repair). Mobile spot repair feasible. Est. R1 500–R3 500 spot repair + blend.
escrowGuarantee: Inspect in direct sun and under streetlight at night from 1 m. If you still see a line, payment stays frozen. You have 7 days to inspect.

articleSections.heading: The fingernail test
articleSections.body: Fingernail across scratch perpendicularly. No catch: clear coat only — polishable. Slight catch: basecoat — touch-up needed. Deep catch and different colour (white/grey/orange): bare metal — full spot repair needed within days before rust.

articleSections.heading: Wet sanding and polishing
articleSections.body: Clear coat scratch is a groove in the lacquer. Wet sanding with 2000-grit smooths edges. Machine polishing restores gloss. Clear coat loses 5–10 microns. If previously polished, may be too thin.

articleSections.heading: DIY vs professional touch-up
articleSections.body: DIY brush-on pen (R150–R300) works for stone chips but leaves a visible lump. Professional: thin coats with fine brush or airbrush, wet-sand flush, clear coat. Result barely detectable.

articleSections.heading: Spot repair process
articleSections.body: Sand the spot, apply primer to metal, basecoat feathering outward, clear coat blended to surrounding panel. The blend line on a good job is undetectable without a paint depth gauge.

articleSections.heading: When full panel respray is needed
articleSections.body: Scratch over 30 cm long and deep over a significant length — spot repair may show a low spot. Sports cars or high-value vehicles need full panel respray for invisible repair.

articleSections.heading: Preventing future scratches
articleSections.body: Ceramic coating reduces micro-scratch visibility but does not prevent deep ones. PPF on high-impact areas blocks physical scratches. Parking away from other cars. Never drying with a dirty towel.

author: Bouul Automotive Services Team

title: Insurance Claims: Step-by-Step Through the Panel Shop Process
subtitle: From accident to back on the road — navigating insurance claims with RMI-accredited shops
problemHeadline: You have had an accident. Now what?
problemBody: After a motor vehicle accident in SA, you have 14 days to claim. The process: SAPS accident number (if injuries or uninsured third party), three-quote assessment, and managing supplements (hidden damage after strip-down). Thousands in write-offs happen because owners do not understand tear-down assessments.
bouulSolution: RMI-accredited panel beaters handle the full process — from assessment to quality check
Assistance with SAPS report, insurer communication, and supplement management
Escrow ensures repair meets standard before final insurance payout release
partsNeeded: Full damage assessment report with photos for insurer
Parts as specified per policy (OEM, OEM-equivalent, or recycled)
Paint inspection and thickness report ensuring blend match
Post-repair inspection certificate (RMI quality checklist)
guidePricing: Varies by damage — excess R1 000–R10 000 typical in SA
aiPromptExample: Rear-ended at a robot in Randburg. Other driver admitted fault, SAPS case number. 2023 Corolla Cross, rear bumper and boot lid damage. Want to use my own panel shop.
aiDiagnosisOutput: Corolla Cross 2023 — rear collision. Visible: bumper, boot lid. Likely hidden: impact bar, tail lights, sensors. Your right: choose any RMI shop. Get 3 quotes (insurer network + Bouul shop), pick best balance.
escrowGuarantee: Before signing insurance release: inspect paint match in sun and at night, check panel gaps symmetrical, test lights and sensors, check boot seals for leaks.
pirbStandard: SANS 10134; RMI Insurance Repair Code of Practice; SAIA guidelines

articleSections.heading: Your rights in the repair process
articleSections.body: You may choose your own repairer. Insurers recommend their network but cannot force you. Non-network shops: insurer sends own assessor. Labour rate difference (R600–R850/h shop vs R550–R650/h insurer cover) is your responsibility. Bouul shops are transparent.

articleSections.heading: The supplement explained
articleSections.body: Hidden damage discovered after strip-down. The panel beater submits a supplement to the insurer, taking 2–5 days to approve. Ask your Bouul shop for a tear-down assessment before the initial quote to minimise supplements.

articleSections.heading: OEM vs aftermarket parts
articleSections.body: Policy specifies OEM, OEM-equivalent, or recycled parts. Comprehensive retail-value policies specify OEM for newer cars. Budget policies specify recycled. If aftermarket does not fit, you may request OEM. Bouul shops show parts before fitting.

articleSections.heading: Paint matching for insurance repairs
articleSections.body: Same paint code varies by age and UV. The shop may need to blend clear into the adjacent panel. Insist on blending in your claim. Bouul escrow verifies blend quality before releasing payment.

articleSections.heading: Write-offs and total loss
articleSections.body: If repair cost exceeds 70–80% of pre-accident value, the car is a write-off. Code 3: repairable and re-registerable. Code 4: scrap. Disagree? Request second opinion from Ombudsman for Short-Term Insurance.

articleSections.heading: The final quality check
articleSections.body: Walk around in sunlight checking paint match and gaps. Close doors/boot — same force as before. Test all lights, sensors, cameras. Test drive for rattles. Release Bouul escrow only after all checks pass.

author: Bouul Automotive Services Team
